MARK BASIS: unlike the after-close passes, close.date IS published at 09-01, but this is an INTRADAY run so every price is the ~10:33 ET regular-session last print - the same basis on both sides of the SPY comparison, stated rather than assumed. COVERAGE 233/233 open symbols priced = 100.0%, ZERO missing, so no survivorship substitution was needed. That is an improvement on the 229/233 (98.3%) the run first reported, and the difference is the process finding below: BABA, DKL, EVLV and RICK are open positions the 08-31 quote file simply did not carry. Screen candidates priced also rose 93/100 -> 97/100 on the same fix. PROCESS FINDING (new, and it aborted the first attempt): run_ghost_oracle.py HYDRATES AT STEP 0, which restores cache/ from claude/live and therefore OVERWRITES any freshly-written cache/ghost_oracle_quotes.json before step 2 reads it. The first run this pass aborted correctly - 'quote cache is not stamped for today (asof=2026-08-31)' - because the file written seconds earlier had been clobbered by the script's own hydrate. The abort is the guard working exactly as intended (it refused to mark 233 names off a stale file). THE FIX, for every future session: PERSIST the fresh quotes to claude/live FIRST (pantheon.persist('ghost_oracle', {'cache/ghost_oracle_quotes.json': ...})), THEN run the script, so its hydrate restores the new file rather than the old one. Writing the quotes locally and running immediately does not work and never did.
